content: Dranath is a fictional herb conceptualized by author Melanie Rawn for her Dragon Prince and Dragon Star trilogies. This herb is exclusively cultivated in the Veresch Mountains of Princemarch and possesses several notable properties. When it is boiled, dried, and powdered, Dranath has the ability to amplify the powers of Sunrunners or sorcerers. Additionally, it aids Sunrunners in crossing water without succumbing to illness. However, in this processed form, the substance is highly addictive, and withdrawal from it is almost invariably fatal to the user. Dranath also has medicinal properties, as it is capable of curing a disease known as The Plague, which affects both humans and dragons. For individuals who are not gifted with magical abilities, the drug acts as a hallucinogen, inducing altered states of perception. Addiction Addiction is the most severe and hazardous side effect associated with Dranath. As the drug is consumed more frequently, the user develops an increasing tolerance, necessitating higher doses to satisfy their cravings. Withdrawal from Dranath results in a range of distressing symptoms, including severe headaches, swelling of the tongue, tremors in the limbs, hypersensitivity to light, chills, generalized body aches, and profound fatigue. In extreme cases of withdrawal, the individual may become nearly insensible. Severe withdrawal symptoms include loss of consciousness, memory lapses, vivid and often sexually explicit dreams, an intense itching sensation both internally and externally, vomiting, muscle cramps, profuse sweating, a foul body odor, and excruciating abdominal pain. The agony experienced during withdrawal can drive the individual to self-harm in an attempt to either obtain more Dranath or escape the unbearable pain. If restrained, the victim’s violent thrashing may result in dislocated joints, such as pulling their arms from their sockets. In some cases, they may even bite off their own tongue. The cumulative effects of withdrawal progressively weaken the body, leading to a state of total exhaustion. At this stage, the heart may fail; if it does, the individual will die unless their heart is restarted, often through cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR), and they are able to resume breathing. Overdosing on Dranath is equally lethal. In such cases, the user experiences sensations akin to drowning, an inability to breathe, and an overwhelming sense of suffocation caused by the drug’s effects.
